ami selects the real machine image, instance_type selects real compute size, key_name enables real SSH access, and tags, covered further shortly, add real, genuine metadata.

blocks.text: 3. A Data Source for the Latest AMI

blocks.content: Hard-coding a real, specific AMI ID genuinely goes stale over time, a data source querying for the latest, real matching image avoids this real problem entirely.
This directly applies the data source concept already covered in the Core Concepts module, reading real, live information rather than storing a static value.
This pattern is genuinely worth adopting as a real, practical default, rather than a hard-coded AMI ID that quietly becomes outdated.
Combining this with the most_recent argument ensures a genuinely current, real image is used on every fresh apply.

blocks.content: 4. user_data: Real, Native Bootstrapping
Recall the When to Use topic from the Provisioners module, user_data is exactly the real, native alternative already recommended there, over reaching for remote-exec.
user_data runs a genuinely real script automatically when the instance first boots, no separate provisioner, or SSH connection, genuinely required at all.
This is worth treating as the real, default choice for initial instance setup, exactly the honest guidance already covered in that earlier module.
Using the file() function, already covered in Built-in Functions, keeps this script in its own, real, separately-maintained file.

A tags argument, a real map of key-value pairs, is worth applying consistently, Name, Environment, and Owner are real, common, practical choices.
This connects directly to terraform.workspace, already covered, tags can genuinely include the active environment automatically.

Recall create_before_destroy from the Meta Arguments module, applied directly here, a real EC2 instance can be replaced with genuinely zero downtime.

This pattern genuinely matters most for instances serving real, live traffic, covered further in the Load Balancer topic ahead.

blocks.content: Recall the connection block from remote-exec, a real key pair, referenced by key_name, is what actually makes SSH access to a live instance genuinely possible.
This key pair must genuinely exist in AWS already, or be created alongside the instance using an aws_key_pair resource, covered briefly here.
Without a real, valid key pair, an instance is created successfully, but genuinely unreachable over SSH at all.

blocks.content: 8. Real Cost Awareness
A real, running EC2 instance genuinely incurs real, ongoing cost, for every hour it exists, regardless of whether it is actually doing useful, real work.
This is worth keeping in mind directly while experimenting, a real, forgotten instance left running is a genuinely common, avoidable, real expense.
